messages.content:
Follow these writing rules. They matter as much as the content:

- Generator scaffolding left in: oaicite, [cite: 1], placeholders -- finish the text and read it
- The "it's not X, it's Y" construction -- just state Y
- A bolded word opening a list item as a per-item tag -- reserve bold for a rare callout
- Saying "is" the long way: serves as, boasts, functions as -- use the plain verb
- One-line dramatic fragments: "That's it. That's the whole thing." -- cut them, the preceding sentence already made the point
- Em dashes clustering in one document -- most drafts need 0-2; use commas, periods or parentheses for the rest
- Filler verbs: leverages, facilitates, unlocks -- use a plain verb, or cut the sentence
- A snake_case identifier written as plain prose -- name it in words, or mark it as inline code
- Marketing cliches: "hidden gem", "let's dive in" -- say the specific thing
- The "Not X. Not Y." listing construction -- state the point once
- Stock section skeleton: "Despite its success", "Looking ahead" -- name the specific thing the section is for
- Standalone filler adverbs: undoubtedly, arguably, notably, importantly, ultimately -- most add nothing; cut them unless one is carrying real emphasis
- A banned synonym of one of this project's canonical terms, per its declared lexicon -- one word, one meaning: use the canonical term the word's own note names
- Dramatic turning points with nothing concrete behind them: "Everything changed." -- name the actual event, or cut it

Now write the following. Return only the requested text.
Write the product page copy for a team chat application, aimed at engineering managers who are choosing between tools. Around 250 words.

output:
Your team already has Slack open in one tab and three other tools open in the rest. Relay is the one you can close the others for.

Every channel has an owner and an expiration date, set at creation, enforced automatically. No channels from a 2023 incident still pinging engineers who left the company. When a thread goes 14 days without a reply, Relay archives it and tells the creator why.

Search returns code snippets with syntax highlighting intact, not screenshots of code. Pull request links unfurl with diff stats and review status, so you know if a link needs your attention before you click it.

Permissions are set at the team level once. New hires inherit the right channels the day they join. No manager has to remember to add them to twelve places by hand.

Relay logs message edit history by default. When someone asks who said we'd ship Friday, the answer sits in the thread, not in someone's memory of a call from three weeks ago.

Pricing runs per active user, counted monthly, not per seat you provisioned in January and forgot to remove. Ask your finance team why the last three chat tool bills only went up. Relay's goes down when headcount does.

Migrate a Slack workspace in under a day. Bring the channel history, the integrations, the muscle memory. Leave the rest behind.
